current.text: Julius Randle and Naz Reid are gone. LaMelo Ball and Jonathan Kuminga have joined the team.
Kyle Anderson, Mike Conley, Joe Ingles and Julian Phillips are also gone.
Donte DiVincenzo will miss most of this season.
Ball, Edwards, McDaniels and Gobert are set as four of the five starters.
The fifth starting spot is open and could change with matchups. Kuminga is listed there, but he is not guaranteed to keep it.
Josh Green is also a candidate for the fifth starting spot.
The team now plays a smaller, guard-heavy lineup. The starting group has little size, and the team is short on defensive rebounding.
The bench is thin and offers little scoring. The second unit has no real ball handler.
Frontcourt depth is close to zero. Joan Beringer is the only backup center behind Rudy Gobert.
Beringer may not be ready for the backup center role.
The team needs wing depth in case of injuries. An injury to a starter would open a big role for a reserve.
With Ball on the team, both Ball and Anthony Edwards should spend less time with the ball.
Ball should cut into Edwards' scoring. Their three-point volume can probably coexist.
Minnesota should be competitive. The expert projects a top 10 defense, a top 10 offense if Ball stays healthy, and 53 wins. Vegas sets the win total at 48.5, eighth in the league.
The team is not expected to tank or rest players late in the season.
Minnesota must make another move to afford the Kuminga signing. Josh Green is the likely player to be traded.
Minnesota plays only 2 games in fantasy playoff week 20, the matchup starting March 15. The experts call it the worst fantasy playoff schedule, and it hurts players like Edwards.
Minnesota has the fewest back-to-backs in the league, so rest risk for its starters is low.

note: Minnesota is a winning team with no tank risk and the fewest back-to-backs in the league, so its starters should play a full load. But only 2 games in week 20 hurts everyone in our playoffs. Ball's arrival should cut Edwards' on-ball time and scoring. The thin frontcourt makes Beringer a real handcuff behind Gobert. Early on, watch who holds the fifth starting spot (Kuminga or Josh Green), whether Beringer is ready, and whether Green gets traded.
